I got an invitation, so I got to see a play in Daehakro for the first time in a long time.
Perhaps due to the coronavirus, there were not many people on the streets even though it was the weekend.
The theater was not far from Exit 1 of Hyehwa Station, and there were signposts all over the place so it wasn't difficult to find.
There was no parking space for spectators, so we had to use a nearby public parking lot.
Unlike last time, I went to building 3 in the basement, which was nice because the bathroom was close by.
It was a play titled Concert in Heaven, and even though I knew the rough synopsis, it was somewhat difficult to become immersed in it until the middle.
It was nice to be able to see the cast's expressions up close because it was a small theater, but it was narrow and the chairs were very uncomfortable.
Because of social distancing, people sat one room apart, so there was less frustration.
When I entered the theater, the air smelled like a warehouse and was unpleasant.
Still, I think I had a good time for the first time in a while because all the actors worked hard until the end.

reviews.author: Jaehyun Lee
reviews.text:
Summary before review
- Parking lot available
- Difficult to find the concert hall building
- 1st floor performance hall that is easy to enter
- Inconvenience of having to go to the bathroom
- Seat discomfort

* This review is about hall 3, so it is not related to halls 1 and 2.

It's a bit difficult to find the building itself.
This is a performance hall located not far from Hyehwa Station. However, it is not easy to find and enter. If you are looking for a performance venue for the first time, get help from the navigation or map.

There is a parking space before entering the venue.
I went in the evening and there wasn't much traffic, but if there's a lot of traffic, the entrance may be hard to see depending on the direction you're visiting. Still, it is expected that most people will be seen lining up.

The performance hall is on the first floor, and it is only about 3 meters from the building entrance to the entrance to the performance hall, so it is less difficult to move around than in other performance halls where you have to climb stairs.

The front, back, left and right sides of the seat are all narrow.
If you are sitting on the edge and someone sitting in the middle seat comes later, it would be better in every way to get up and move out of the way. The time of my review is in the winter, and it is difficult to put your arms around each other comfortably when wearing padding. Depending on your personality, you may watch with a rigid posture.

The way to the bathroom can be a bit inconvenient.
It is difficult to access directly because you have to turn around a bit from the entrance of the building, and you have to go past the entrance to the men's restroom to get to the women's restroom.

The performance venue was uncomfortable, but the play ‘Hakana’ was fun!

reviews.text:
It is one of the top tier arcades in Seoul for rhythm gamers.
It is quite large, consisting of a second floor, first floor, and basement.
On the first floor, there are Drummania, Nostalgia, Shintaego, Easy2, Waka, My My DX, Reflect, and Guitar Freaks. On the second floor, there are several Sabol, Two-Deck, Pop'n, and U-Beat.
In the basement, there are game machines such as pump, ddr, dance rush, and other competitive games in addition to league games.

The owner is friendly and if you are playing a game, you can
You can also make coffee with it.
It consists of three floors, but the area per floor is a bit small, so the devices are close together, so the sound tends to overlap slightly. But it's not a big concern. It would be a good idea to bring earphones.

The location is about 5 minutes away from Hansung University Station and has good accessibility. There is a convenience store not far away, so if you are thirsty or hungry, you can go there and get a bite to eat.

There is a water purifier, but only one cup is provided, so I recommend bringing your own cup.

Personally, I think it's the best arcade in Seoul, and I hope this place doesn't go bankrupt and keeps going.

This is a slightly special place. This is where the works of the late Lee Nam-gyu, who worked as a glass artist in Korea, are installed.
Glass blocks (Daldver) and face glass that give a strong pictorial feel were installed. Dalde Vert is a technique developed in France. Tap the edges of a 2-3cm glass block evenly.
If you make it into a distorted shape and place it on a synthetic resin and concrete mold,
It will shine like a jewel. Teacher Lee Nam-gyu can be said to be stronger in pictorial aspects because he was a painter who focused on painters more than Dalde Vert.

reviews.author: Ignatius Park
reviews.text:
Hyehwa-dong Cathedral is the third parish established in Seoul, following Myeong-dong Cathedral and Jungnim-dong Yakhyeon Cathedral.
In 1927, the Benedictine monastery that was located at the site of the parish moved to South Hamgyong Province and took over the cathedral building.
The current cathedral building was built in 1960.
Hyehwa-dong Cathedral is as famous as a treasure trove of sacred art as it is for its history.
In particular, the murals and stained glass decorating the back of the altar, the painting of the 103rd saint, the Last Judgment on the outside of the wall, and various icons are of high artistic value.
In addition, Hyehwa-dong Cathedral enshrines the remains of four saints, including Bishop Ember, Mo Mi-soo, Chastan, and Father Kim Dae-geon.
